summary: Cyber Rights: Defending Free speech in the Digital Age is a non-fiction book about cyberlaw by free speech lawyer Mike Godwin, first published in 1998 by Times Books and republished as a revised edition by The MIT Press in 2003. Written in the first person, it covers the legal issues and history of free speech on the Internet and documents the author's experiences defending online speech. Its central thesis is that the remedy for the abuse of free speech is more speech, and Godwin argues that Internet expression decisions also affect free speech in other media under the First Amendment.
one_line: Mike Godwin's 1998 book on cyberlaw and free speech on the Internet, with a 2003 MIT Press revised edition.
key_facts: Cyber Rights: Defending Free speech in the Digital Age is a non-fiction book about cyberlaw written by free speech lawyer Mike Godwin.
The book was first published in 1998 by Times Books.
The book was republished in 2003 as a revised edition by The MIT Press.
Mike Godwin graduated from the University of Texas School of Law in 1990.
Mike Godwin was the first staff counsel for the Electronic Frontier Foundation.
The book is written with a first-person perspective.
The book offers a background in the legal issues and history pertaining to free speech on the Internet.
The book documents the author's experiences in defending free speech online.
The book puts forth the thesis that "the remedy for the abuse of free speech is more speech".
Godwin emphasizes that decisions made about the expression of ideas on the Internet affect freedom of speech in other media as well.
Freedom of speech in other media is granted by the First Amendment to the United States Constitution.
